answer: Picture identities as a coastal lagoon: a new agent must deposit refundable collateral at a metered wharf before its transactions count, and withdrawal is throttled by a ledger-wide rate limit. Sybils that spin up a thousand fake selves can only drain the shared quota at the same aggregate speed one honest agent could, so splitting into clones buys no extra throughput. Reputation then erodes like karst under acid wherever an identity's attested work and its staked deposit diverge, draining the fakes first.
